realm.name: admin
realm.description: Full access: view visitor logs, command robot movement, modify robot parameters.

realm.name: operator
realm.description: Can view visitor logs and command robot movement. Cannot modify robot parameters.

realm.name: robot
realm.description: M2M identity for the simulated robot. Sends data only; cannot read visitor logs or modify its own parameters.

clients.name: Simulated Robot (M2M)
clients.description: OAuth2 Client Credentials client for the simulated reception robot, per EF-05.

clients.name: Supervision Dashboard
clients.description: OAuth2 Authorization Code client for human dashboard users (admin/operator), per Sprint 3 auth flows.

_comment_service_account_role: The robot-service client's built-in service account must be assigned the 'robot' realm role after import — Keycloak's realm-export JSON does not reliably wire service-account role mappings on first import across versions. Do this once via: Admin Console > Clients > robot-service > Service Account Roles > Assign role > robot. Sprint 3 docs will include the equivalent kcadm.sh / Admin REST command for reproducibility.
_comment_secrets: Placeholders like ${env.ROBOT_CLIENT_SECRET} are resolved by Keycloak's config value providers at import time, sourced from environment variables — never hardcode real secrets in this file (ENF-05/ENF-08). Demo user passwords are marked temporary so they must be changed on first login.
